transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-15 14:05 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood Security), Maya Chen (CISO, Aurora Bio), Carlos Ruiz (Head of MLOps), Lena Park (Lead Infra), Tom Becker (Procurement)

Summary (auto-generated):
High-level security discovery focused on compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), SSO/SAML and RBAC expectations, encryption and KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and retention, and a decision between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics: SOC2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, Audit logs, Encryption/KMS, Data retention, VPC/private deployment, Dedicated capacity pricing

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions eng and Ethan from security.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Thanks, Jordan. Want to be respectful of the hour, we have a hard stop at 2:50 our time but should be fine.
[00:16] Jordan Miller: Perfect, quick agenda — understand Aurora's security requirements, map them to Hosted / Dedicated / Private options, and list specific docs you want.
[00:26] Carlos Ruiz: Quick note, our timeline for a POC is Q3, but security sign-off is the gating factor. So we need to understand cryptographic controls, key management, and auditability.
[00:36] Priya Kapoor: Sure. To ground things, are you primarily looking at hosted Redwood API or are you leaning dedicated / private?
[00:42] Lena Park: We're evaluating all three. Hosted is attractive for dev speed, but the CISO team is skeptical on data residency and key controls. Dedicated might be the sweet spot if we can get isolated pools and BYOK. Private on-prem is last resort.
[00:55] Ethan Zhao: Got it. On BYOK, we do support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM-backed flows in our Private offering; Dedicated supports KMS sidecar patterns for key wrapping. 
[01:08] Maya Chen: When you say KMS sidecar, does that mean keys never touch Redwood's control plane? We need proof that plaintext keys aren't in your environment.
[01:17] Ethan Zhao: Right, for Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS — you keep root keys in your KMS/HSM, and we perform envelope encryption. The control plane has only wrapped keys. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the keys stay fully under your control, obviously. I'll share the architecture diagram.
[01:29] Tom Becker: Also, what about SOC 2 and ISO? We need the Type II report and a high-level gap analysis for ISO 27001.
[01:36] Jordan Miller: We can share SOC 2 Type II and our ISO attestation summary — I'll attach both. There's also our security whitepaper and pen test summary.
[01:42] Maya Chen: Do you do annual pen tests and do you have bug bounty?
[01:45] Priya Kapoor: Yes, annual pen tests, periodic third-party red teaming; we also run a private bug-bounty program via a vetted vendor. I should note some of the language in the reports gets redacted for customer confidentiality.
[01:57] Carlos Ruiz: Good. Audit logs — we need immutable logs with retention controls and export capabilities to our SIEM (Splunk). Is there an API or S3 export?
[02:06] Ethan Zhao: We expose audit logs through both streaming to customer S3 buckets and via an audit API. Logs include request metadata, model used, timestamps, and decisioning flags. For Hosted we retain logs by default for X days, and you can pull exports; for Dedicated and Private you get longer retention options and can ship them to your SIEM directly.
[02:24] Lena Park: Are logs tamper-evident? We need to show chain-of-custody for incident reviews.
[02:29] Ethan Zhao: We support signed logs and append-only storage with integrity checks; for Private you can enable immutable storage on your side. For Dedicated we can configure write-once buckets and also provide digest signatures.
[02:40] Maya Chen: Data residency — our models will be used on PHI-ish clinical notes, can't leave EU. Do you have region restrictions?
[02:47] Jordan Miller: Yes, we offer regional deployments. Hosted has EU regions, Dedicated can be provisioned in your preferred region, and Private on-prem handles it too. We also have data processing addenda for healthcare customers.
[02:57] Carlos Ruiz: Encryption in transit and at rest? TLS for in-flight but what about at-rest on GPU nodes?
[03:03] Priya Kapoor: All in-transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we use disk encryption and application-layer envelope encryption using KMS. For GPUs we keep KV cache encrypted in memory and on-disk swap encrypted; some customers ask about encrypting GPU memory — that's trickier but we mitigate with tenant isolation and kernel-level protections.
[03:21] Maya Chen: Can you describe RBAC? Our teams need strict separation: devs can call non-prod models, ops can deploy model versions, sec only sees logs.
[03:29] Jordan Miller: We support role-based access with granular roles. You can map to SAML groups and use SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. Roles cover model access, billing, deployment, and audit viewing.
[03:39] Lena Park: SSO — SAML or OIDC? We use Okta and Azure AD.
[03:43] Priya Kapoor: SAML and OIDC both supported, Okta and AAD are standard. We also do SCIM for user provisioning. Some small transcription issues in logs sometimes label SAML as "SAML2" in old exports, but functionality is solid.
[03:56] Tom Becker: For procurement, can you provide an SLA on uptime and incident response? Also, incident notification policy?
[04:03] Jordan Miller: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets and a dedicated support lane. We provide 24/7 incident response for enterprise customers, with on-call and response time commitments. We'll share the SLA doc.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Backup and restore? If a model or dataset is corrupted, can you prove point-in-time recovery?
[04:18] Priya Kapoor: We snapshot model artifacts and have regular backups of customer artifacts. For Private deployments you manage backups; for Dedicated we can set RPO/RTO targets per contract.
[04:28] Carlos Ruiz: How about data deletion and retention? We need the ability to purge data and evidence of deletion for compliance.
[04:34] Ethan Zhao: We support retention windows and deletion APIs. For Hosted we have default retention of 90 days for raw request bodies unless customers opt-in to longer retention for debugging. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention as low as 0 days on request and provide deletion receipts.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Can you redact or disable logging for specific endpoints? For PHI flows we may want no persistent raw logs.
[04:54] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have configurable logging levels and PII scrubbing. You can opt to disable raw payload logging and only keep metadata. That's common for healthcare customers.
[05:05] Jordan Miller: Quick note on model fallbacks — if you use a smaller model for cost, we still log model switches; those are part of audit.
[05:12] Lena Park: Tokenization — do you store embeddings or prompts? We plan to store embeddings for search experie— experience but raw prompts contain clinical notes.
[05:21] Ethan Zhao: Embeddings are treated as derived data, but we can treat them as PII if you ask. We can also encrypt embeddings at rest with customer keys.
[05:30] Tom Becker: Any major compliance certifications besides SOC 2 / ISO? HIPAA attestation?
[05:35] Jordan Miller: We have a HIPAA BAA for specific offerings; need to sign the BAA and meet certain guardrails. I'll include the BAA template.
[05:43] Maya Chen: Do you have product-level secure configurations we must enable for HIPAA?
[05:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we have a HIPAA hardening guide that includes disabling request logging for PHI, enabling BYOK, and network egress restrictions.
[05:56] Carlos Ruiz: Network — do you support VPC peering or private connectivity?
[05:59] Ethan Zhao: Both. We support VPC peering, PrivateLink and dedicated interconnects for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted can use private endpoints in some regions.
[06:10] Maya Chen: How are secrets stored? Do you have HSMs in your control plane?
[06:15] Ethan Zhao: Control plane secrets are stored encrypted and keys are rotated regularly. For customers requiring HSM-backed keys, we integrate with your HSM via KMS. For Hosted, keys are managed by Redwood but we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts.
[06:28] Priya Kapoor: Small caveat, sometimes logs mislabel KMS regions in older exports, we've fixed the tooling but FYI.
[06:34] Lena Park: On the encryption front, can you walk through an example of request flow with envelope encryption?
[06:38] Priya Kapoor: Sure. Client encrypts payload keys via customer's KMS or we use our API that wraps with your KMS; the runtime unwraps per-request with ephemeral keys, processes inference, and re-encrypts outputs. Plaintext never written to persistent storage. We'll share a diagram and sequence flow.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Pen test results — do you have remediation timelines and CVE handling process?
[07:03] Ethan Zhao: Yes, standard process: critical issues are remediated within SLA windows (depends on severity), we notify customers and publish CVE statuses.
[07:11] Tom Becker: For procurement, need a list of required controls to include in the SOW and SLA.
[07:16] Jordan Miller: We'll provide a security annex template with required controls and SOW language.
[07:21] Carlos Ruiz: A couple of technical questions — how do you handle KV cache expiration and does it get persisted? If we have PII in prompts, we want to ensure caching doesn't store it beyond necessary.
[07:31] Priya Kapoor: KV cache is ephemeral and kept in memory; we persist only when we're doing checkpointing for long-running sessions and those artifacts are encrypted. You can request zero-persistence mode for sensitive workloads.
[07:44] Lena Park: For Dedicated POC, what's the lead time to spin up a dedicated pool in EU?
[07:48] Jordan Miller: Typically 2-4 weeks depending on capacity. We can expedite for pilot customers. Pricing will be in the Dedicated quote.
[07:56] Maya Chen: Onboard checklist for security team — what should they expect?
[07:59] Ethan Zhao: We'll run a security intake: review of architecture, gap analysis against your policies, data flow diagrams, pen test review, access review, and finally a runbook for incident response.
[08:12] Jordan Miller: Let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Please summarize.
[08:16] Jordan Miller: Action items: I will send SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary plus BAA template (Jordan by 2025-07-17). Ethan will send KMS/HSM integration notes and the architecture diagrams (Ethan by 2025-07-20). Lena will send Aurora's retention policy and preferred retention windows (Lena by 2025-07-18). Carlos will share workload profile and peak token rates for the POC (Carlos by 2025-07-22). We'll schedule a technical deep dive next week with Priya and your infra team.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Sounds good. One more ask — can you provide a sample audit log export anonymized? That would help our compliance team.
[08:46] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we'll scrub PII and provide a sample export.
[08:50] Jordan Miller: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up over email with the attachments and proposed times for the deep dive.
[08:57] Tom Becker: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[09:00] End of recording (note: timestamps in transcript are approximate, small transcription artifacts present).
